property_summary: Only calls to setL1BlockValues originating from the contract's DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT succeed; calls from any other sender must revert.

For any successful call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the contract's public timestamp equals the _timestamp argument passed; the mutant can violate this when a later assignment reverts (or would have reverted) so timestamp may remain unset or differ.

For any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the reference contract always sets timestamp to the provided _timestamp even if a later storage write would revert; the mutant (which writes timestamp last) can leave timestamp unset when one of the earlier assignments triggers a revert (e.g., due to a malicious batcherHash setter that reverts on certain values), so there exist inputs where the mutant's timestamp != the provided _timestamp while the reference always equals it.

For any inputs and a depositor caller, C always sets timestamp to the _timestamp argument even if a subsequent external write to another contract would revert; the mutant that assigns timestamp last can be made to revert on a later assignment by providing a specially crafted batcherHash that points to a malicious contract causing a revert, so there exist fuzzed inputs where the mutant's timestamp is not set while the reference always sets it.

For any depositor call, the reference C always sets the storage variable `number` to the provided _number argument (reads via public getter) regardless of other external interactions; the mutant that moves `timestamp` assignment later can be made to revert during a later external write causing timestamp to differ while `number` in the mutant may still differ — therefore asserting that after a completed call number == _number distinguishes the implementations.

For any depositor call to setL1BlockValues, if the call completes successfully then the reference C always sets timestamp to the provided _timestamp (reads via public getter); the mutant can be made to complete successfully while leaving timestamp unequal to _timestamp when a later storage write would have reverted (because timestamp was written earlier in reference but last in mutant), so there exist fuzzed inputs and a malicious callee that make the mutant violate this rule.
Only the designated depositor account can make setL1BlockValues change c.basefee (i.e., if caller != depositor then basefee remains unchanged).

property_summary: Calls to setL1BlockValues initiated by any account other than the DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT always revert (so reverted == true for non-depositor callers).
Only calls to setL1BlockValues made by the depositor address may succeed (non-depositor calls always revert).
If the caller equals the contract's DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT then the call to setL1BlockValues must succeed (reverted == false), otherwise it must revert (reverted == true).

For every call to setL1BlockValues the stored basefee equals the provided _basefee (P: basefee == _basefee for all inputs); the mutant violates this by storing _basefee + 1 for some fuzzed _basefee values.
